The petitioner-bank being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said Order dated 08.01.2004 filed Civil Revision Case No.6 of 2004 before the learned District Judge, Kurigram which was summarily rejected by judgment and Order dated 29.3.2004. Thereafter, the petitioner-bank filed Artha Rin Appeal No.1 of 2004 under Section 41 of the Ain against the selfsame Order dated 08.01.2004 before the learned District Judge, Kurigram and after hearing, the learned District Judge dismissed the appeal vide his judgment and Order dated 01.9.2004 as being barred by limitation. 

 6. Mr. S. M. Atikur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner-bank submits that the Executing Court had no jurisdiction to exercise power under Section 47(1) of the Artha Rin AM, 2003 as the execution case was filed according to the provision of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. He also submits that on the wrong advice of the learned Advocate of the Court below, the petitioner-bank at the initial stage filed Civil Revision and being unsuccessful filed the appeal in accordance with law against the impugned order but as there was no provision in the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 to condone the delay, the appeal was dismissed on the ground of limitation and the Rule issued in Civil revision was also discharged on the same point and as there was no other alternative forum, the petitioner filed the instant writ petition as this Division has jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution to see the propriety and legality of the impugned order passed by the Adalat.
